subject: english-language
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the AQA GCSE English Language specification, what is the Spoken Language Endorsement usually presented as by students?
questions.explain: The endorsement requires students to give an individual formal presentation or speech on a chosen topic.

questions.q: How is the Spoken Language Endorsement reported in relation to the GCSE grade?
options: It forms 20% of the final GCSE grade
It is reported separately and does not count towards the 9-1 grade
It is added to Paper 2 marks
questions.explain: The endorsement is reported separately from the 9-1 GCSE grade and does not contribute to it.

questions.q: Which of the following grades can a student be awarded for the Spoken Language Endorsement?
questions.explain: Students are awarded Pass, Merit, Distinction or Not Classified for the endorsement.

questions.q: In what kind of setting must the presentation for the endorsement be delivered?
options: An informal chat with a friend
questions.explain: AO7 requires students to demonstrate presentation skills in a formal setting.

questions.q: Why is the presentation required to be prepared and delivered individually rather than as a group?
options: Group work is banned in all GCSE subjects
So each student's own presenting skills can be assessed
Because Standard English cannot be used in groups
questions.explain: Individual delivery allows the assessor to judge each student's own presentation ability against the criteria.

questions.q: Which of the following would most improve a candidate's mark for presenting?
options: Reading the entire speech word-for-word from a script in a monotone
Organising ideas clearly and engaging the audience through tone and structure
Speaking as quickly as possible to fit more in
questions.explain: Effective presenting involves clear organisation and audience engagement, not simply reciting a script.

questions.q: A student chooses to present on 'Why local libraries should be protected'. To present most effectively, they should:
options: Structure the talk with a clear opening, developed points and a strong conclusion
List random facts with no ordering
Avoid making any eye contact with the audience
questions.explain: A clearly structured presentation with a defined opening, development and conclusion best demonstrates presenting skills.

questions.q: Which choice of topic is most suitable for the formal presentation task?
options: A topic the student can research and speak about substantively
A topic with no available information
An offensive topic to shock the audience
A blank topic decided during the talk
questions.explain: Choosing a topic the student can develop and sustain supports a strong, well-organised formal presentation.

questions.q: After delivering the presentation, what are students expected to do as part of the endorsement?
options: Listen and respond to questions and feedback
questions.explain: AO8 requires students to listen and respond appropriately to questions and feedback on their presentation.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on listening and responding appropriately to spoken language, including questions and feedback?
questions.explain: AO8 covers listening and responding appropriately to spoken language, including questions and feedback on presentations.

questions.q: What does 'responding appropriately' to audience questions primarily require?
options: Understanding the question and giving a relevant, considered answer
Answering only with a single word every time
questions.explain: Appropriate responses show the student has listened, understood the question and answered relevantly.

questions.q: Why is listening carefully to a question before answering important in this task?
options: It wastes time so the session ends sooner
It ensures the response is relevant and directly addresses what was asked
It is not assessed at all
It allows the student to change the topic
questions.explain: Careful listening allows a relevant, focused answer, which is central to AO8.

questions.q: A student is asked a question they did not fully expect. The best response is to:
options: Take a moment to consider, then give a thoughtful, relevant reply
Answer with 'I don't know' and stop
questions.explain: Pausing to consider and then responding relevantly demonstrates strong listening and responding skills.

questions.q: During questioning, an audience member disagrees with a point in the presentation. The strongest response would:
options: Acknowledge the point and respond with reasoning or evidence
questions.explain: Engaging with the challenge and justifying one's view demonstrates appropriate, considered responding.

questions.q: Which assessment objective concerns the effective use of spoken Standard English in speeches and presentations?
questions.explain: AO9 requires students to use spoken Standard English effectively in speeches and presentations.

questions.q: What is meant by 'Standard English' in this endorsement?
options: Any regional dialect the student prefers
The widely accepted form of English using conventional grammar and vocabulary
Only formal written English with no speaking
English spoken only in a particular accent
questions.explain: Standard English is the conventional form using recognised grammar and vocabulary, and is not tied to any accent.

questions.q: Which of these best reflects effective use of spoken Standard English?
options: 'We was going to discuss three points today'
'We were going to discuss three points today'
questions.explain: Using the standard verb form 'we were' demonstrates conventional Standard English grammar.

questions.q: Using Standard English in a formal presentation is important mainly because it:
options: Helps communicate clearly and appropriately in a formal context
Prevents the use of any complex vocabulary
questions.explain: Standard English supports clear, appropriate communication suited to the formal nature of the task.

questions.q: A student's draft opening reads: 'Right, so basically I ain't gonna bore yous.' To meet AO9, they should revise it to:
options: 'Right, so basically I ain't gonna bore yous'
'Today I will discuss a topic I hope you will find interesting'
'Ain't nobody got time for boring talks'
questions.explain: The revised opening uses Standard English grammar and vocabulary suitable for a formal presentation.

questions.q: Which sentence would best demonstrate spoken Standard English when answering a question?
options: 'That is a good question, and I would argue that the evidence supports my view'
questions.explain: This response uses standard grammar and appropriately formal vocabulary, meeting AO9.

specSource: AQA GCSE English Language (8700) specification; Non-examination Assessment: Spoken Language Endorsement
